label: final copy step (mostly L=3,6,7), sparse token-specific tail
explanation: Extremely sparse reset-gate tail (0.03% of steps). Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (~94% of mass) on the very last output step (to_go == 0), concentrated in sequences of length 3, 6 and 7 (t=5, 11, 13); never fires in the original or delimiter phase, nor on early copy steps. Within that context it fires on only ~1% of eligible steps: the choice depends on a sparse conjunction of specific tokens (input q/t/d/f/m/1 is enriched; strongest cases are L=3 with first token d/c/q/v and input t/q/m/d, e.g. d t m <DEL> d [t]). Adding these token lists raises precision only at a large recall cost and does not form a coherent rule, so precision stays very low. Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.02), largest for L=3.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: q, t, 1, x; t=7: t, q, d; t=13: q, 1, d, f) and the first original token (most: j, b, c, d, p, u; least: m, f, i, n); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, recall_idx=6, L=3.
